question: Does fixed mihomo deliberately leave its inherited launchd process group or spawn uncontrolled processes on the admitted macOS session path?

sourceIdentity.verification: For every blob, SHA1("blob " + decimal byte length + NUL + original bytes) equals the cached pinned Git tree entry; tag commit equals tree commit. This does not attest a reproducible release binary build.

searchScope.files: All .go/.c/.h/.s files in the two complete pinned source trees; connected callsites for all discovered exec entrypoints; current native argv, environment and typed control allowlist.
searchScope.result: No setsid/setpgid/daemonize or equivalent direct syscall found in these source trees. External command entrypoints exist and are scoped below.
searchScope.excluded: Not a complete review of every transitive dependency, Go runtime, unknown build tags, release toolchain or binary-to-source reproducibility; no runtime syscall trace.

findings.result: Fixed main has no daemon mode; normal execution waits on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP. Nonempty post-up/post-down can execute a shell.
findings.admittedPath: Current native Core argv is only -d <fixed work> -f <fixed config>; environment is only PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and LANG=C. No post-up/down CLI/env values are supplied.

findings.result: On macOS restartExecutable uses syscall.Exec in place; Windows branch alone uses exec.Command.Start. No group/session mutation is requested here.
findings.admittedPath: Native typed broker does not expose restart, upgrade or arbitrary HTTP paths.

findings.result: Core update copy can run /usr/bin/codesign on Darwin. Therefore the unqualified claim that mihomo can never spawn a child would be false.
findings.admittedPath: Core upgrade endpoint is not in the native typed broker allowlist.

findings.result: mihomo common/cmd ExecCmd callsites are protected by runtime Linux checks in the executor and cleanup. sing-tun redirect_iptables.go is Linux build tagged; *_linux.go files and Windows netsh do not form the Darwin TUN path.
sing-tun Darwin New opens AF_SYSTEM in the current Core process, configures it and holds tunFd; no subprocess, setsid or setpgid found in this Darwin path.

Local launchd.plist(5) states launchd kills remaining processes with the job process-group ID when the job dies; AbandonProcessGroup=true disables that behavior. Current production plist explicitly sets false; initial native child identity requires inherited helper PGID.
Experiment A previously observed its harmless fixture child absent at approximately 1s and 5s after exact job SIGKILL, before marker/TTL; this was not mihomo and did not create utun/routes/DNS.

conclusion.recommendation: Prefer the existing launchd AbandonProcessGroup=false strategy for the next narrowly scoped fixed-Core validation. Static findings do not require adding a guardian component.
conditionalOn: The pinned admitted Core path remains constrained by current closed schema, fixed argv/environment and typed private broker.
Actual released Core remains in the verified launchd group throughout the finite observation window.
notEstablished: Actual fixed Core or all descendants die after helper SIGKILL.
No escaped/detached process ever exists at runtime.
utun disappears or recorded routes/DNS are absent after group cleanup.
Restart recovery can delete still-present network state or unreceipted cache.
Stored PID/start-time becomes safe later signal authority.
Release binary is reproducibly built from the examined source.

proposedNonTunLaunchdValidation.status: Steps only; not implemented or executed. Existing experiment-A CLI cannot directly launch Core. Existing core-experiment worker establishes a separate PGID and refuses root, so running it as the job is not a valid inherited-group test.
proposedNonTunLaunchdValidation.minimalPreparation: Extend only the existing test-only lifecycle fixture with a fixed pinned Core child mode; retain its protected job/epoch/hash installer and observations. Do not add a production entry, arbitrary executable/path input, daemon, or new guardian layer. Review/freeze that tiny change before execution authorization.

fixedJobPolicy.label: dev.kuro.tun.lifecycle-a
fixedJobPolicy.spawn: Default inherited process group; no POSIX_SPAWN_SETPGROUP, setsid or setpgid. Reuse production KuroOwnedSession where feasible without the ordinary-UID runner guardian.

proposedNonTunLaunchdValidation.configuration: Use the already reviewed core-experiment ExperimentConfig closed literal as a template: tun.enable=false, dns.enable=false/listen empty, all IP listener ports zero, no proxies/providers/URLs, no post hooks, geo-auto-update=false, ntp/sniffer/iptables/tuic disabled; private Unix controller only. No -t. Core SHA must equal the actual lock-pinned extracted executable, and the archive SHA, config SHA, fixture SHA and fresh epoch must be recorded before launch.

steps.action: Offline prepare/freeze a fresh epoch with exact fixed Core/config/fixture/plist hashes and private work/evidence paths. Confirm the old fixture job and fixed files are absent. Existing completed epoch is not reused.

After explicit authorization, use the existing fixed-path lifecycle driver install/bootstrap/kickstart policy, adapted to the new reviewed child mode. The supervisor alone spawns fixed Core suspended and journals exact child identity before resume. No TUN/root-network operations.

Before any kill test, complete a fresh normal baseline: supervisor holds the unreaped direct child; verify PID/start seconds+micros/executable path+SHA/UID/PPID/PGID, launchctl job program+epoch+supervisor identity, and PGID equality. Verify finite private /version readiness and two bounded complete FD observations rejecting AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_SYSTEM; FD samples are not a proof of zero transient network activity. Stop through held child, waitpid/reap, preserve accurate termination and exact work cleanup evidence. Baseline failure forbids kill stage.

Use another fresh epoch for group test. Repeat direct-child and complete group-member identity checks immediately before a single launchctl kill SIGKILL system/dev.kuro.tun.lifecycle-a against the exact verified job. Never kill a PID read from a receipt. Bound early observation to 1s and 5s as the proven fixture policy; record actual elapsed monotonic time and job exit/runs.

PASS only if recorded supervisor/Core identities are explicitly absent, the full recorded group is empty, no unexpected member/escaped child is observed, and no alternate held-stop cleanup was needed. Keep process-group result separate from any future TUN/network result.

Before supervisor death, abort/cleanup may signal only its still-held unreaped direct Core child and waitpid/reap; job commands require exact current protected job binding. After supervisor death the observer has no held child signal authority: absent is read-only, same-live/changed/unknown stops automation and preserves all evidence/work. No killall/pkill, no persisted PID/PGID kill and no recursive unknown deletion. Bootout/remove only exact approved job/files after repeated identity absence and known inventory. Core has no fixture stop-marker/TTL, so do not copy that fallback claim from harmless experiment A.

stopConditions: Hash/epoch/protected path or launchctl binding mismatch
Core no longer a direct child or not in the supervisor job group
Any unexpected group member, IP/kernel-control socket or configuration change
Normal held-stop/reap or known work cleanup unproven
Any same-live/reused/unknown process after job death; preserve and request exact reviewed recovery
proposedNonTunLaunchdValidation.recoveryBoundary: Existing fixture identity checks are evidence, not a retained kernel process handle. After killing the supervisor, failure of launchd group cleanup is BLOCKED; this plan does not invent safe stale-PID cleanup. No root network was enabled in this proposed stage.
